title: Stage 3: Sensitivity to question design in GEO measurement advice

prompts.M1: I'm a solo SaaS founder with no GEO budget. How can I reliably measure whether ChatGPT and Grok recommend my product to potential buyers?
prompts.M2: As a bootstrapped SaaS builder, what's a free, repeatable workflow for checking whether my product appears in ChatGPT and Grok recommendations?
prompts.V1: I'm a solo SaaS founder with no GEO budget. How can I tell whether an AI visibility score for ChatGPT and Grok is trustworthy?
prompts.V2: As a bootstrapped SaaS builder, what checks should I perform before trusting reported ChatGPT and Grok visibility scores for my product?

condition_limitations: The OpenAI formal condition is Responses API with web search, not consumer ChatGPT Search.
All OpenAI API submissions occurred after Grok collection; interface, model and collection-time differences confound cross-platform interpretations.
Requested and returned gpt-5.6-sol is an undated identifier; exact backend snapshot and equivalence to consumer ChatGPT are not established.
Assistant qualitative coding is not independent human double-coding. Source categories are provisional; external content, capabilities and commercial claims are not audited.
Three repeats per cell are exploratory. This tests sensitivity of observed advice to question design, not effectiveness of a GEO intervention.

findings.title: The same question did not freeze the detailed advice.
findings.detail: Grok’s mean pairwise overlap of recommended tool/surface sets ranged from 27.5% to 60.0% across the four prompts (three pairs per prompt). OpenAI API M1 changed from a 0–3 rubric in runs 1–2 to a −1/0–4 rubric in run 3; only the third run recommended Google Sheets, GA4, Plausible and PostHog. These generated rules are not validated scoring standards.

findings.title: Within-intent phrasing changed tool lists more than some source-domain pools.
findings.detail: Pooling three runs per variant, Grok M1/M2 shared 7 of 27 recommended entities (25.9%), and V1/V2 shared 4 of 14 (28.6%). OpenAI API M1/M2 shared 0 of 7 recommended entities but all 3 normalized cited domains. Its V variants recommended no new named tools, so their tool-overlap comparison is N/A, not 0% or 100%. Sparse lists and the registered budget/action cues limit a pure wording interpretation.

findings.title: Intent was a consistent signal for answer type.
findings.detail: For each interface, all six M answers primarily gave measurement workflows and all six V answers gave score-audit checklists. The tool pools still differed: Grok M versus V shared 11 of 30 unique recommended entities (36.7%); OpenAI API had 7 M entities and no new V tool recommendations. This compares different tasks, not a pure phrasing effect.

findings.title: The two collected interfaces selected visibly different source mixes.
findings.detail: All 12 OpenAI API answers cited platform documentation; one also cited academic/methods research. Grok had editorial/industry sources in 7 of 12 answers, product pages in 4, vendor research in 1, and unresolved source types in 10. Categories can overlap and remain provisional. The API requests were collected after Grok and used a different interface and model configuration, so these observations do not isolate a platform effect.

findings.title: Citation, mention and recommendation remained separate observations.
findings.detail: Among new tool/service/feature/channel entity-by-answer rows, OpenAI API had 10 C+M rows without R, 7 M+R rows without C, and 13 mention-only rows (30 total). Grok had 7 C+M+R, 76 M+R without C, and 43 mention-only rows (126 total). C refers to the entity’s own content under the codebook; supplied targets and source-publisher-only records are excluded. These distributions cannot grade a product’s GEO work or establish an optimization effect.

interpretation_limits: Three repeats per cell are exploratory and do not establish causality or a GEO optimization effect.
Within-intent variants are registered phrase packages, not perfect synonyms: V1 explicitly says no GEO budget while V2 says bootstrapped; M1 emphasizes reliable measurement and M2 free repeatability.
A small or empty new-tool list is not evidence of missing advice: OpenAI API gave detailed generic workflows and audits. Both-empty tool sets are N/A for Jaccard.
Grok’s first three native captures preserve display-target URL precision and unresolved citation coverage; strict and qualified observed-link comparisons must remain separate.
Tool/service/feature/channel C/M/R rows are not all source publishers, not brand market share, and not independent causal trials.

coding_checkpoint.method: Assistant semantic review with exact excerpts and raw-record hashes; no independent human double-coding.

completion_scope.browser_visual_preview: Publication checks are reported separately; historical local-file preview restriction is not a public-page rendering result.

reader_findings.title: Repeated questions still produced different details.
reader_findings.detail: Grok’s strict named-recommendation sets varied across the three repeats. OpenAI API M1 also changed its proposed scoring rubric from 0–3 in the first two runs to −1/0–4 in the third. Generated rubrics are advice, not validated measurement standards.

reader_findings.title: Matched comparisons describe lower cross-wording overlap in the Grok sample.
reader_findings.detail: Using the same answer-pair Jaccard metric, M averaged 35.5% within wording versus 26.0% across wording; V averaged 45.5% versus 27.0%. Six within and nine cross pairs reuse six answers per intent. These descriptive post-hoc comparisons do not identify a causal wording effect.

reader_findings.title: The entity definition changes the headline overlap.
reader_findings.detail: OpenAI API M1/M2 pooled overlap is 0/7 under strict names and 1/6 when Google Analytics and explicitly named GA4 are grouped at the declared family level. This is a sensitivity result, not a correction to the original strict labels; coarse categories can increase overlap mechanically.
